synthesis.series-family-structures-give-.formal:
Work at the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction with the textures and the order of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-rule}: $M_{e} = c(\J + \delta_{c}(E + X_{e}))$, $\mD = d(\J + \delta(E + X_{\nu}))$, $M_{R} = \alpha\Pi + M_{3}\J/3$, $E = e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf T}$, $P_{12}$ the exchange of $e_{1}, e_{2}$, each $X_{s}$ odd under $P_{12}$, now allowed complex. Call the series' family structures $\mathbb{1}$, $\J$, $\Pi$, $E$ (Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation}), $u'\wedge s$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.residual-s2-fixes-120-family-form}) and the cyclic shift $S$, $Se_{j} = e_{j+1}$, with $S^{\mathsf T}$. Let $A$ be the matrix of $v \mapsto u'\times v$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(One odd line.)} The $P_{12}$-odd part of the complex span of the series' family structures is $\C A$, with $A = S - S^{\mathsf T}$ and $S + S^{\mathsf T} = \J - \mathbb{1}$. $A$ spans the sign representation of $S_{3}$, $PAP^{\mathsf T} = \mathrm{sgn}(P)A$, which occurs exactly once among the $3 \times 3$ family matrices; it is antisymmetric, fixed by the $3$-cycles and odd under every transposition. Without the shift, which enters only through the circulant reading of (ii) and is not a premise of the store, the $P_{12}$-odd part of the span of $\mathbb{1}$, $\J$, $\Pi$, $E$ and $u'\wedge s$ is zero.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The channel phase on that line, circulant reading.)} The circulant (numbers, and $\C$, are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$) $C = \mathbb{1} + \tfrac{\lambda}{2}(e^{I_{4}\delta}S + e^{-I_{4}\delta}S^{\mathsf T}) = (1 - \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\cos\delta)\mathbb{1} + \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\cos\delta\,\J + I_{4}\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\sin\delta\,A$ has eigenvalues $1 + \lambda\cos(\delta - 2\pi k/3)$ on the Fourier vectors $f_{k}$, the components of the projected Koide vector of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(iii) up to scale and labelling. So if the face family lines are read as the Fourier lines of a flavour basis, the channel phase is the coefficient of the sign line, odd under every residual $S_{2}$, and it breaks $S_{3}$ to $\mathbb{Z}_{3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Moduli.)} In the compression $B_{s} = \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} 2/3 & x_{s}\\ y_{s} & 0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ of that proposition, a symmetric odd $X$ gives $y = x$, an antisymmetric one $y = -x$, a Hermitian one $y = \bar{x}$, and $X = \gamma A$ gives $x = \sqrt3\gamma = -y$ for every complex $\gamma$; in all of these $|x| = |y|$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Sum rule for complex charged stages.)} For $B = \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} k & x\\ y & 0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ with $k > 0$ and complex $x, y$, the light left singular vector depends only on $k$, $|x|$, $|y|$, and for $|x| = |y|$ it makes the angle $\theta$ with $\tan^{2}\theta = \sigma_{2}/\sigma_{1}$ with the odd axis. Hence, with any complex charged stage with $|x_{e}| = |y_{e}|$ and a real one-type neutrino stage, $|U_{e1}| \ge \cos(\theta_{e} + \theta_{\nu})$ and the sum rule $\Delta \le \arctan\sqrt{m_{e}/m_{\mu}} + \arctan(m_{1}/m_{2})^{1/4}$ holds; under the inequality of Premise (H), taken as a hypothesis of this clause, $\Delta < 21.6^{\circ}$, excluding the measured solar angle.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Consequence.)} No second stage built linearly from the series' family structures, in the charged sector with any complex coefficient and in the neutrino sector with a real one, reaches the measured solar angle under (H) at the breaking lemma's order. The stage the data need has $|y| \ne |x|$ in some sector: an $S_{2}$-odd symmetric part (a standard-representation component) together with an antisymmetric part at a non-Hermitian relative phase, which the series' structures do not supply; products such as $AE = (1,-1,0)\,e_{3}^{\mathsf T}$ would.
\end{enumerate}
For a complex neutrino coefficient the light neutrino angle is not a function of the moduli, and the result makes no statement there. \emph{Note (pointer).} For neutrino stages of one type in modulus ($|x| = |y|$ in the light-plane block), which is what the 10 couplings of the $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion supply, the complex case is decided in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.complex-neutrino-stages-keep-the-solar-sum-rule}: a phase raises the neutrino tilt at most by the factor $(1 + \sqrt{\rho})/(1 - \sqrt{\rho})$, to $\tan^{2}\theta_{\nu} = \tfrac{11}{90}$ (about $19.3^{\circ}$) at $\rho = \tfrac{1}{100}$, and the solar angle stays below $23.3^{\circ}$ under (H) at the breaking lemma's order; stages with $|x| \ne |y|$ remain outside both results.
synthesis.series-family-structures-give-.technical:
The stored decoupling result says the second stage of the family breaking must be odd under the exchange of the first two families. This result asks whether the series' own family structures contain such a stage. They are few: the unit, the democratic matrix, the breaking direction, the one antisymmetric form allowed at the first stage, and the cyclic shift that appears when the Koide vector is written as the spectrum of a circulant matrix. All but the shift are even. The shift contributes one odd line, the cross-product matrix of the democratic vector, which is the sign representation of the permutation group: antisymmetric, unchanged by cyclic relabellings and reversed by every exchange. In the circulant reading of the Koide parametrisation the channel phase, the number that encodes the muon-to-electron ratio, is exactly the coefficient of this line, so the phase is an odd stage for every choice of residual exchange and breaks the permutations down to the cyclic ones.

That line cannot be the second stage the solar angle needs. The stored sum rule bounds the solar angle for one-type stages on real textures; here the bound is extended to complex charged-lepton stages, because the light state's angle depends only on the moduli of the two off-diagonal entries of the light-plane block, and symmetric, antisymmetric and Hermitian stages all give entries of equal modulus. Since the series' line is antisymmetric, any multiple of it is one type, and under the hierarchical premise, with a real neutrino coefficient and at the breaking lemma's order, the solar angle stays below about twenty-two degrees. The stage the data ask for needs a symmetric odd part as well, at a relative phase that is not Hermitian; the series' structures do not contain one, though products of them do.
synthesis.series-family-structures-give-.lay: The theory explains the three generations of matter through a symmetry among them that is broken in stages, and the measured mixing angles of neutrinos require a particular kind of second stage, one that treats the first two generations oppositely. This result looks through the theory's own building blocks for such a stage and finds exactly one: a twisting pattern that is reversed by swapping any two generations. When the electron, muon and tau square-root masses are read as the spectrum of a cyclic matrix, it is also where the theory's one free angle, the number behind the muon being about 207 times heavier than the electron, lives. But this pattern is of the wrong shape to produce the large solar mixing angle: the bound on that angle holds for it, even with complex phases in the charged-lepton part (the neutrino part with complex phases is only explored numerically). So, if the second stage is hierarchical in the sense the theory assumes, the stage the data require is not among the theory's existing structures.

synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-ru.formal:
Take the textures of Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation} at the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction $E = e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.theta23-at-s3-s2-direction}, with a second stage in each sector: $M_{e} = c\bigl(\J + \delta_{c}(E + X_{e})\bigr)$, $\mD = d\bigl(\J + \delta(E + X_{\nu})\bigr)$, $M_{R} = \alpha\Pi + M_{3}\J/3$, where each $X_{s}$ is real and odd under the exchange $P_{12}$ of the first two families, $P_{12}X_{s}P_{12} = -X_{s}$ (the $S_{2} \to 1$ stage). Work at the Lemma's order, where the light states and masses of each sector come from the compression $B_{s}$ of $E + X_{s}$ to $u'^{\perp}$, and let $\hat{b}_{e} = (1,1,-2)/\sqrt6$, $\hat{b}_{o} = (1,-1,0)/\sqrt2$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] In the basis $(\hat{b}_{e}, \hat{b}_{o})$, exactly, $B_{s} = \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} 2/3 & x_{s} \\ y_{s} & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$, and $\Pi A\Pi A^{\mathsf{T}}\Pi = (\Pi A\Pi)(\Pi A\Pi)^{\mathsf{T}}$. So the charged light states are the left singular vectors of $B_{e}$ with $m_{e}/m_{\mu} = \sigma_{2}/\sigma_{1}$, and the light neutrino states are the left singular vectors of $B_{\nu}$ with $m_{1}/m_{2} = (\sigma_{2}/\sigma_{1})^{2}$. Symmetric $X_{s}$ gives $y_{s} = x_{s}$, antisymmetric $X_{s}$ gives $y_{s} = -x_{s}$.
\item[(ii)] For every real $B = \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} k & x \\ y & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ with $k \neq 0$ and distinct singular values $\sigma_{1} > \sigma_{2}$, the angles $\theta_{L}$, $\theta_{R}$ of its heavy left and right singular vectors from the first axis satisfy $\sigma_{2}/\sigma_{1} = |\tan\theta_{L}\tan\theta_{R}|$, and $|\theta_{L}| = |\theta_{R}|$ when $y = \pm x$.
\item[(iii)] (The sum rule.) With $\Delta$ the angle between the lightest charged-lepton state and the lightest neutrino state, so that $|U_{e1}| = \cos\Delta$ at this order, $\Delta = |\theta_{L}^{\nu} - \theta_{L}^{e}|$. If each $X_{s}$ is purely symmetric or purely antisymmetric,
\[
\Delta \;\le\; \arctan\sqrt{m_{e}/m_{\mu}} \;+\; \arctan\,(m_{1}/m_{2})^{1/4} ,
\]
and if $m_{1}/m_{2} \le 0.01$ (the inequality of Premise (H), Premise \claimref{neutrino.h-second-stage-hierarchical}, taken here as a hypothesis of the clause) then $\Delta < 21.6^{\circ}$ and $|U_{e1}|^{2} > 0.865$, against $|U_{e1}|^{2} = c_{12}^{2}c_{13}^{2} \le 0.711$ at the three-sigma edges of the global fit. A second stage of one type in each sector, the $120$-like antisymmetric or the $10$/$126$-like symmetric alone, is excluded at this order.
\item[(iv)] The measured angle therefore needs, in at least one sector, an $S_{2}$-odd second stage with both a symmetric and an antisymmetric part and left-right lopsidedness bounded below. Exactly, for the block of (ii), $y/x = \tan\theta_{L}(1 + \tan^{2}\theta_{R})/\bigl(\tan\theta_{R}(1 + \tan^{2}\theta_{L})\bigr)$. With the charged sector of one type and $m_{1}/m_{2} \le 0.01$, the neutrino sector needs $|\tan\theta_{L}^{\nu}/\tan\theta_{R}^{\nu}| > 2.95$, equivalently in the texture entries $|y_{\nu}/x_{\nu}| > 2.35$; so $|y_{\nu}| \ne |x_{\nu}|$, which by (i) needs both a symmetric part $(x + y)/2$ and an antisymmetric part $(y - x)/2$.
\end{enumerate}
Since the antisymmetric family coupling is the one the grade-three direction supplies on the series' registered route, (iv) says the solar angle asks that this direction and a symmetric one act together in one sector's second stage; it does not derive their ratio.
synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-ru.technical:
At the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction both small lepton angles vanish exactly (the vector $(1,-1,0)$ lies in both kernels), so the solar angle must come from the second stage $S_{2} \to 1$. This result computes what that stage can do at the order of the breaking lemma, where each sector's light pair is governed by a $2 \times 2$ block $\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} 2/3 & x \\ y & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ in the light plane; the zero is exact because the second stage is odd under the surviving exchange. The neutrino's light block is the square of the same compression, so its light states are the left singular vectors and its mass ratio is the square of the singular-value ratio.

A $2 \times 2$ block with a zero corner obeys $\sigma_{2}/\sigma_{1} = |\tan\theta_{L}\tan\theta_{R}|$. When the second stage is purely symmetric or purely antisymmetric the left and right tilts agree, so each sector's left tilt is fixed by its own hierarchy: $\sqrt{m_{e}/m_{\mu}}$ for the charged leptons and $(m_{1}/m_{2})^{1/4}$ for the neutrinos. The angle between the two lightest states is at most the sum, under 21.6 degrees once Premise (H) holds, while the data need about 32 to 36. The solar angle therefore needs a lopsided second stage, symmetric and antisymmetric parts together in one sector with left tilt about three times the right (texture entries in ratio above 2.35) at least on the neutrino side. Scope: the Lemma's order is the perturbative branch, where the democratic seesaw term dominates and the compressions give the light states; on that branch Proposition \claimref{synthesis.theta23-at-s3-s2-direction} already excludes a near-maximal $\theta_{23}$. On the root past the peak, where $\theta_{23}$ can be met, the compression reading fails and the one-type exclusion rests only on a numerical exploration of the full textures (one-type maximum 23.5 degrees, lopsided breakings reaching 50 degrees), not on this proof.
synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-ru.lay: The framework explains why one family of each kind is much heavier than the other two, but the mixing between electron-type and other neutrinos has to come from a second, smaller symmetry breaking. This result shows that if that second breaking is of a single simple kind in each sector, the largest mixing it can produce is set by two small mass ratios, the electron-to-muon ratio and the ratio of the two lightest neutrino masses, and, at the leading order of the breaking, comes out below about 22 degrees. The measured angle is about 33 degrees. So the second breaking must combine two different kinds of coupling in a lopsided way, which the framework's preferred route happens to contain but does not yet fix.

synthesis.stored-fits-are-models-of-not-.technical:
Hypothesis (U) puts the neutrino's leading Dirac eigenvalue at the common rank-one value of all sectors at the ceiling, read either as the top's or as the bottom's. The Standard-Model paper's fits on its Pati-Salam route reproduce all eighteen fitted observables with the equal-weight premise held exactly, and they leave the neutrino Dirac matrix to the couplings. Evaluated exactly from the stored coupling sets, its leading singular value at the intermediate scale is about $0.054$, $3.16$, $5.00$ and $3.12$ GeV in the four sets, while the top and bottom there are $92.45$ and $1.365$ GeV.

No set is near either reading: all are at least eighteen times below the top and at least a factor $2.2$ away from the bottom, and they spread over a factor above ninety. So (U) is not a consequence of the premises the fits satisfy; it is an additional input. A common running factor to the ceiling cannot change that conclusion for more than one set. On the set without a $120$ the leading value is fixed mainly by the $126$'s second-family entry, $\hat{f}_{22} \approx 0.025 + 0.011I_{4}$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$), rather than by the mixing ratio $\hat{f}_{23}$, so a rank-one model of $\hat{f}$ does not describe these sets.
synthesis.stored-fits-are-models-of-not-.lay: An assumption of the series, Hypothesis (U), fixes the neutrino's ordinary mass at the highest energy scale to be the top quark's mass or the bottom quark's. The series' unified-theory fits reproduce all measured quark and lepton masses and mixings without using this assumption. This result reads off, exactly, what those fits give for the neutrino's ordinary mass: at the intermediate scale of the fits, between about 0.05 and 5 GeV depending on the fit, never close to the top quark's 92 GeV or to the bottom quark's 1.4 GeV there; whether the same holds at the highest scale is argued, not computed. So the assumption is not forced by the rest of the theory and the data; it is an extra choice that the series would have to justify separately.

proofs.main:
\emph{Step 1 (the matrices).} Proposition \claimref{standard-model.fits-record-level} records four representative fits under Hypothesis (S), Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}, Premise (EW) and the Pati-Salam $v_{R}$; their coupling sets $(Y, Z, f, h, w_{u}, w_{d}, c_{u}, c_{\nu}, c_{d})$ are stored digit for digit in the Standard-Model paper's script (Part M, obs:anglefits) \cite{ButlerT12}, and the check copies them as decimal strings, read as exact rationals with complex numbers as pairs. As in that script, Premise (EW) is imposed by setting $Y_{33} = 3w_{u}f_{33}$, and the Dirac mass matrices are $M_{u} = Y + w_{u}f + c_{u}h$, $M_{\nu} = Y - 3w_{u}f + c_{\nu}h$, $M_{d} = Z + w_{d}f + c_{d}h$ by the Fact. Since $h$ is antisymmetric, $(M_{\nu})_{33} = Y_{33} - 3w_{u}f_{33} = 0$ exactly, which the check confirms.

\emph{Step 2 (exact singular values).} For each matrix $M$ the check forms $A = MM^{\dagger}$, verifies that its trace, sum of principal two-by-two minors and determinant are real, and brackets the largest root $\sigma_{\max}^{2}$ of $\det(t - A)$ by Sturm sequences over $\Q$: exactly one root above $\mathrm{lo}^{2}$ and none above $\mathrm{hi}^{2}$. This gives (i) for $M_{u}$ and $M_{d}$ (the fits' targets $m_{t}(M_{I}) = 92.45$ GeV and $m_{b}(M_{I}) = 1.3651$ GeV, the latter met to the fits' two-percent tolerance in the third set, $1.36493$) and (ii) for $M_{\nu}$. The record-level table's largest $|M_{\nu}|$ entries ($0.04$, $2.9$, $4.0$, $2.2$ GeV) are consistent: each lies between $\sigma_{\max}/3$ and $\sigma_{\max}$.

\emph{Step 3 (comparison).} With $m_{t} = 92.45$ and $m_{b} = 1.3651$ GeV, each upper bracket times $18$ is below $m_{t}$; the first set's upper bracket times $2.2$ is below $m_{b}$, and the other three lower brackets exceed $2.2\,m_{b} = 3.003$; and the largest lower bracket exceeds $90$ times the smallest upper one. This is (iii). synthesis.theta23-at-s3-s2-direction.formal:
Take the textures of Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation} at the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction $E = e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ in both sectors: the charged-lepton matrix $c(\J + \delta_{c}E)$ with $\delta_{c} = 0.286$ (exact singular values give $m_{\mu}/m_{\tau} \in (0.0594, 0.0596)$), $\mD = d(\J + \delta E)$, $M_{R} = \alpha\Pi + M_{3}\J/3$ with $\alpha, M_{3} > 0$, and $m_{\nu} = \mD M_{R}^{-1}\mD^{\mathsf{T}}$; write $|U_{\tau 3}|^{2} = (x_{\tau} \cdot x_{3})^{2}$ for the unit heavy eigenvectors of the two sectors.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Exactly, $m_{\nu} = \lambda_{D}E + \lambda_{M}\hat{w}\hat{w}^{\mathsf{T}}$ with $w = (\J + \delta E)(1,1,1)^{\mathsf{T}} = (3, 3, 3 + \delta)$, $\hat{w} = w/|w|$, $\lambda_{D} = 2d^{2}\delta^{2}/3\alpha$ and $\lambda_{M} = d^{2}|w|^{2}/3M_{3}$. The vector $(1,-1,0)$ is in the kernel of $m_{\nu}$ and of the charged matrix ($m_{1} = m_{e} = 0$), so both heavy eigenvectors lie in the plane spanned by $(1,1,0)$ and $e_{3}$, and $|U_{\tau 3}|^{2}$ is the squared cosine of the difference of their angles in that plane.
\item[(ii)] The heavy neutrino eigenvector is nearer $\hat{w}$ than $e_{3}$ exactly when $\lambda_{M} > \lambda_{D}$. At fixed $\delta$ the ratio $m_{2}/m_{3}$, as a function of $M_{3}/\alpha$, peaks at $\lambda_{M} = \lambda_{D}$ with value $\tan^{2}(\varphi/2)$, $\varphi$ the angle between $w$ and $e_{3}$ (at $\delta = 0.286$: $M_{3}/\alpha = 176.0$ and $m_{2}/m_{3} \in (0.240, 0.241)$). The two roots of $m_{2}/m_{3} = \rho$ below the peak are exchanged by $\lambda_{M} \mapsto \lambda_{D}^{2}/\lambda_{M}$, and their heavy eigenvectors are reflections of each other across the bisector of $\hat{w}$ and $e_{3}$.
\item[(iii)] On the perturbative branch $\lambda_{M} \ge \lambda_{D}$, for every $|\delta| \le 1$ of either sign, $|U_{\tau 3}|^{2} > 0.76$: its least value, attained at $\delta = 1$ and $\lambda_{M} = \lambda_{D}$, lies in $(0.7687, 0.7688)$, the heavy eigenvectors there about $28.7^{\circ}$ apart. At the instance of Remark \ref{rem:branch} ($\delta = \delta_{c}$, $M_{3}/\alpha = 66$, $m_{2}/m_{3} \in (0.168, 0.172)$) it exceeds $0.96$, the two heavy eigenvectors about $11^{\circ}$ apart (tilts of about $13^{\circ}$ and $3^{\circ}$, in the same sense).
\item[(iv)] Past the peak, at the remark's size $|\delta| = 0.286$ and $m_{2}/m_{3} \in (0.168, 0.172)$: with $\delta = +\delta_{c}$ ($M_{3}/\alpha = 469.5$), $|U_{\tau 3}|^{2} \in (0.55, 0.58)$, just outside the window; with $\delta = -\delta_{c}$ ($M_{3}/\alpha = 530.7$), $|U_{\tau 3}|^{2} \in (0.50, 0.55)$, inside the measured window $(0.39, 0.55)$ of the global fit \cite{NuFIT2024}, the window Observation \claimref{neutrino.mixing-none-leading-order} reads from the record.
\end{enumerate}
So the open number of that Observation is settled at the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction: a breaking of exactly the remark's size $|\delta| = 0.286$ supplies a near-maximal $\theta_{23}$, but only on the root past the peak of $m_{2}/m_{3}$, where the lemma's remainders dominate and $\alpha/M_{3} \approx 1.9 \times 10^{-3}$, and only with the Dirac neutrino breaking opposite in sign to the charged lepton's; on the perturbative branch the paper takes, it cannot.
synthesis.theta23-at-s3-s2-direction.technical: At the direction that breaks the three-family permutation symmetry to a two-family one, the light-neutrino matrix is exactly the sum of two rank-one pieces, one along the third family's axis from the Dirac breaking and one along a nearly democratic vector from the heavy Majorana mass. Both lepton sectors then keep the two-family symmetry, so their heavy eigenvectors lie in one plane and the large mixing angle is the difference of two tilts in that plane. For a sum of two rank-one pieces the heavier eigenvector lies nearer whichever piece is larger; the ratio of the two light masses peaks where the pieces are equal, and the two values of the Majorana ratio that give the measured mass ratio are mirror images, with mirror-image eigenvectors. On the root the paper uses, where the Majorana piece dominates, the neutrino's heavy eigenvector stays near the democratic direction, as the charged lepton's does, and the mixing is small: at the paper's instance about eleven degrees, and at most about twenty-nine degrees for any breaking up to one in size, against the forty-two to fifty-one required. On the mirror root the neutrino eigenvector swings towards the third family's axis, and at the remark's size, with a Dirac breaking opposite in sign to the charged lepton's, the separation reaches forty-four degrees, inside the observed range.
synthesis.theta23-at-s3-s2-direction.lay: Neutrinos change type as they travel, and one of the measured mixing angles is close to its largest possible value. The series' structure gives no mixing at first approximation, and asked whether a small correction of the size it suggests could supply the large angle. For the simplest form of the correction this result answers exactly. On the branch the series chose, no: the angle comes out about four times too small. On a second branch, where a different heavy mass ratio reproduces the same neutrino mass ratio, yes at that size, provided the correction to the neutrinos has the opposite sign to the one for the charged leptons. Whether that second branch is acceptable is now the question.

synthesis.two-loop-running-cannot-fix-ma.formal:
Take the chains of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chain} (real bidoublet, complex bidoublet, complex bidoublet with the $(15,2,2)$), with $x = \ln(M_{I}/M_{Z})/2\pi$, $y = \ln(M_{U}/M_{I})/2\pi$, the matching $a_{1} = \tfrac35 a_{2R} + \tfrac25 a_{4}$, $a_{2} = a_{2L}$, $a_{3} = a_{4}$ of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.matching-traces} and the inputs of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run}. Write the Majorana coupling of the $(10,1,3)$ as $-\mathcal{L} \supset \tfrac12 f_{ij}\,\psi^{c}_{i}\psi^{c}_{j}\Delta_{R}$ with $\psi^{c} = (\bar{4},1,2)$ and canonically normalised components, so that $M_{R} = v_{R}f$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}), and a Dirac-type coupling as $y_{ij}\,\psi_{i}\psi^{c}_{j}\Phi$ with $\psi = (4,2,1)$ and $\Phi$ in a representation $R \subset (4,2,1)\otimes(\bar{4},1,2)$. Apply Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-loop-yukawa-gauge-terms} on $M_{I} < \mu < M_{U}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Selection rule.)} A Dirac-type coupling contributes $Y_{4} = \tfrac14\dim R\,\mathrm{Tr}(yy^{\dagger})\,(1,1,1)$ to $(SU(4), SU(2)_{L}, SU(2)_{R})$, universal also after the matching; it shifts $\alpha_{U}^{-1}$ and leaves $M_{I}$ and $M_{U}$ unchanged. The scalars light on $(M_{I}, M_{U})$ other than the $(10,1,3)$, the bidoublet ($\dim R = 4$) and the $(15,2,2)$ ($\dim R = 60$), couple only in this way, whichever $10$, $120$ or $126$ they descend from. The $(10,1,3)$ coupling contributes $(\tfrac{15}{4}, 0, \tfrac{15}{2})\,\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})$, matched $v = (6, 0, \tfrac{15}{4})\,\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})$: it is the only Yukawa coupling of the chains that moves the scales at two loops.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The running never fixes the coupling.)} With $\varepsilon = \langle\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})\rangle/16\pi^{2}$, the average over $\ln\mu$ on $(M_{I}, M_{U})$, the running reads $a_{i}(M_{Z}) = a_{U} + b_{i}^{\mathrm{SM}}x + (b_{i}^{\mathrm{eff}} - \varepsilon v_{i})\,y + u$, with $u$ the universal Dirac-type shift. For each chain its determinant is $D_{0} + \tfrac{201}{4}\varepsilon$, the coefficient $\tfrac{201}{4} = -[6(b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{3} - b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{2}) + \tfrac{15}{4}(b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{2} - b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{1})]$ the same for every chain (it involves only the columns $1$ and $b^{\mathrm{SM}}$), with $D_{0} = \tfrac{364}{15}, \tfrac{386}{15}, \tfrac{114}{5}$, positive for every $\varepsilon \ge 0$, so the three measured couplings fix $(a_{U}, M_{I}, M_{U})$ uniquely as functions of $\varepsilon$ and do not fix $\varepsilon$; $M_{I}$ rises strictly with $\varepsilon$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sizes, one-loop baseline.)} $d\ln M_{I}/d\,\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})$ lies in $(0.09, 0.10)$, $(0.08, 0.09)$ and $(0.10, 0.11)$ for the three chains, against a move of $\ln M_{I}$ between $0.03$ and $0.05$, opposite in sign, for $\alpha_{s} \to \alpha_{s} \pm 0.0009$. If $M_{I}$ were supplied (or $M_{U}$, for instance from proton decay), the measured couplings would fix $\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})$ near one, but only to within more than $\pm 0.3$ per standard deviation of $\alpha_{s}$. So the statement "never" in (ii) is the count with the three gauge couplings as the only data.
\end{enumerate}
So the two-loop Yukawa terms break the scaling symmetry of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.majorana-scale-free-on-pati-salam-route} only into a one-parameter family $M_{I}(f)$: along it $m_{3} \propto 1/(|\lambda|\,v_{R}(\lambda))$ is strictly monotone, so the observed $m_{3}$ is still the one datum that values the Majorana scale, and the running of the gauge couplings supplies no relation that fixes it. The algebraic companion, filed alongside, is synthesis.majorana-element-is-null-blade-no-frozen-point-condition: no invariant algebraic condition on the Majorana element fixes the scale either.
synthesis.two-loop-running-cannot-fix-ma.technical: The problem asked whether two-loop gauge running with Yukawa terms, which first feel the Yukawa couplings, could fix the Majorana coupling $f$ on the Pati-Salam chain once the weak angle is measured. It cannot. The Yukawa term of the imported two-loop Fact weights each fermion by its quadratic Casimir; for a coupling of a left-handed to a right-handed multiplet the weights come out equal for $SU(4)$, $SU(2)_{L}$ and $SU(2)_{R}$, so every Dirac-type coupling shifts the unified coupling only and none of the scales. Only the Majorana coupling of the $(10,1,3)$, which joins two right-handed multiplets, moves $M_{I}$ and $M_{U}$. But the chain already uses the three measured couplings to solve for three unknowns ($\alpha_{U}$, $M_{I}$, $M_{U}$), and the Yukawa term keeps that system linear and nonsingular for every value of the coupling: the running returns $M_{I}(f)$, not $f$. With the three gauge couplings as the only data the coupling stays free. If $M_{I}$ were supplied from elsewhere, the running would determine the trace of $ff^{\dagger}$, but at the one-loop baseline a unit trace moves $\ln M_{I}$ by only a few times the shift from a one-sigma change of the strong coupling, so the trace would be fixed only to about $0.4$ per sigma of $\alpha_{s}$.
synthesis.two-loop-running-cannot-fix-ma.lay: At very high energies the strengths of the forces drift, and at the second level of precision they also feel the couplings of matter to the Higgs-like fields. One might hope that this drift, compared with the measured strengths, pins down the coupling that sets the heavy neutrino mass. It does not. Couplings that join left-handed to right-handed matter push all three forces equally and change nothing but their common unified strength. The heavy neutrino coupling does move the unification scales, but the measured strengths are already used up in fixing those scales, so the drift tells us the scales once the coupling is known, never the coupling. The heavy neutrino mass therefore stays a number read off the observed neutrino masses.

proofs.main:
\emph{Conventions.} Fermions are two-component, $\kappa = \tfrac12$, and Yukawa couplings are written $-\mathcal{L} \supset \tfrac12 Y^{a}_{jk}\psi_{j}\psi_{k}\phi_{a} + \mathrm{h.c.}$ with real scalars $\phi_{a}$, as in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-loop-yukawa-gauge-terms}. A complex scalar with components $\Phi_{c} = (\phi_{c1} + I_{4}\phi_{c2})/\sqrt{2}$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$) along an orthonormal basis $T^{c}$ of its place in the fermion bilinear, coupled as $\tfrac12(y\otimes T^{c})_{jk}\psi_{j}\psi_{k}\Phi_{c}$, has $Y^{c1} = (y\otimes T^{c})/\sqrt2$ and $Y^{c2} = I_{4}(y\otimes T^{c})/\sqrt2$, so $\sum_{a}Y^{a}Y^{a\dagger} = yy^{\dagger}\otimes\sum_{c}T^{c}T^{c\dagger}$. For the $(10,1,3)$ the entry along $\nu^{c}\nu^{c}$ is a basis element, so $\langle\Delta_{R}\rangle = v_{R}$ gives $\tfrac12 v_{R}f\,\nu^{c}\nu^{c}$, that is $M_{R} = v_{R}f$ as in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}. A Dirac-type coupling $(y\otimes T^{c})_{(iA)(jB)}\psi_{iA}\psi^{c}_{jB}\Phi_{c}$ fills the two off-diagonal blocks of $Y^{a}$, and $\sum_{a}Y^{a}Y^{a\dagger}$ is $yy^{\dagger}\otimes\sum_{c}T^{c}T^{c\dagger}$ on the $\psi$ block and $y^{\mathsf T}\bar{y}\otimes\sum_{c}T^{c\mathsf{T}}\bar{T}^{c}$ on the $\psi^{c}$ block.

\emph{(i)} Each of $\psi = (4,2,1)$ and $\psi^{c} = (\bar4,1,2)$ has eight components $(a, \alpha)$. Since $\Phi$ spans an irreducible representation and $\psi$, $\psi^{c}$ are irreducible, $\sum_{c}T^{c}T^{c\dagger}$ is invariant on each eight-dimensional space and so, by Schur's lemma, $(\dim R/8)\,\mathbb{1}_{8}$, its trace being $\sum_{c}\mathrm{Tr}\,T^{c}T^{c\dagger} = \dim R$. The check confirms it on explicit orthogonal bases: $30/8$ for the $(10,1,3)$ (symmetric in the $SU(4)$ pair and in the $SU(2)_{R}$ pair), $4/8$ for the $(1,2,2)$ ($\delta_{ab}\otimes E_{\alpha\beta}$), $60/8$ for the $(15,2,2)$ (off-diagonal $E_{ab}$ and traceless diagonals), on both blocks. With $C_{2}(4) = \tfrac{15}{8}$, $C_{2}(2) = \tfrac34$, $d(SU(4)) = 15$, $d(SU(2)) = 3$:
\[
Y_{4}^{i} = \frac{1}{d(G_{i})}\mathrm{Tr}\bigl[C_{2}^{i}(F)\,Y^{a}Y^{a\dagger}\bigr] = \frac{\dim R\,\mathrm{Tr}(yy^{\dagger})}{d(G_{i})}\bigl(C_{2}^{i}(\psi) + C_{2}^{i}(\psi^{c})\bigr),
\]
which is $\dim R\,\mathrm{Tr}(yy^{\dagger})\cdot(\tfrac{15/4}{15}, \tfrac{3/4}{3}, \tfrac{3/4}{3}) = \tfrac14\dim R\,\mathrm{Tr}(yy^{\dagger})(1,1,1)$, because $\psi$ and $\psi^{c}$ both carry the fundamental of $SU(4)$ and each carries the doublet of exactly one $SU(2)$. The matching gives $(\tfrac35 + \tfrac25)\cdot\tfrac14\dim R\,\mathrm{Tr}(yy^{\dagger}) = \tfrac14\dim R\,\mathrm{Tr}(yy^{\dagger})$ for $a_{1}$ and the same for $a_{2}$, $a_{3}$: a universal vector. For the $(10,1,3)$ only $\psi^{c}$ couples, $\mathrm{Tr}\,YY^{\dagger}$ over $\psi^{c}$ is $8\cdot\tfrac{30}{8}\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger}) = 30\,\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})$, so $Y_{4} = (30\cdot\tfrac{15}{8}/15,\ 0,\ 30\cdot\tfrac34/3)\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger}) = (\tfrac{15}{4}, 0, \tfrac{15}{2})\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})$, matched $(\tfrac35\cdot\tfrac{15}{2} + \tfrac25\cdot\tfrac{15}{4},\ 0,\ \tfrac{15}{4}) = (6, 0, \tfrac{15}{4})$. The $(10,1,3)$ cannot couple as $\psi\psi^{c}$ ($4\otimes\bar4$ holds no $10$), and by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pati-salam-representation-theory-survival}(b) and Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element} the only scalars light on $(M_{I}, M_{U})$ in the chains are the bidoublet, the $(10,1,3)$ and, where named, the $(15,2,2)$; the $(\overline{10},3,1)$ is not light.

\emph{(ii)} By the Fact, the Yukawa part of the gauge running is $d\alpha_{i}^{-1}/d\ln\mu \supset \kappa Y_{4}^{i}/16\pi^{3}$ (from $\beta(g) \supset -2\kappa g^{3}Y_{4}/(4\pi)^{4}$ and $d\alpha^{-1}/d\ln\mu = -8\pi\beta/g^{3}$); integrated over $\ln(M_{U}/M_{I}) = 2\pi y$ it is $\kappa\langle Y_{4}^{i}\rangle y/8\pi^{2}$, which in $a_{i}(M_{Z}) = a_{U} + b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{i}x + b^{\mathrm{eff}}_{i}y$ enters, after the matching of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.matching-traces} at $M_{I}$, as $-\varepsilon v_{i}y - u$ with $\varepsilon = \langle\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})\rangle/16\pi^{2}$, $v = (6, 0, \tfrac{15}{4})$ and $u$ universal. (The sign of $u$ is immaterial.) Here $b^{\mathrm{SM}}$ and $b^{\mathrm{eff}}$ are the one-loop sums of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices} and the $a_{i}(M_{Z})$ the inputs of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run}. For fixed $\varepsilon$ and $u$ the system is linear in $(a_{U}, x, y)$ with matrix rows $(1, b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{i}, b^{\mathrm{eff}}_{i} - \varepsilon v_{i})$; its determinant is affine in $\varepsilon$, computed as $D_{0} + \tfrac{201}{4}\varepsilon$ with $D_{0} = \tfrac{364}{15}, \tfrac{386}{15}, \tfrac{114}{5}$ for the three chains, positive for every $\varepsilon \ge 0$; expanding along the third column, the coefficient of $\varepsilon$ is $-\det[\mathbb{1}, b^{\mathrm{SM}}, v] = -[6(b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{3} - b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{2}) + \tfrac{15}{4}(b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{2} - b^{\mathrm{SM}}_{1})] = \tfrac{201}{4}$, which involves only the columns $\mathbb{1}$ and $b^{\mathrm{SM}}$ and so is the same for every chain (checked directly). So Cramer's rule gives one solution for every $\varepsilon \ge 0$; it back-substitutes, and the check verifies on $\varepsilon \in \{0, \tfrac18, \dots, 3\}$ (the cap $\varepsilon \le 3$ is singular values of $f$ at most $4\pi$) that $x$ rises strictly, and that a universal $u$ shifts $a_{U}$ by $-u$ and leaves $x$, $y$ unchanged. Three data, the measured $a_{i}(M_{Z})$, are used up by the three unknowns $(a_{U}, x, y)$ at each $\varepsilon$; no equation remains for $\varepsilon$. The two-loop gauge terms of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chain}(1) add to this system terms of relative order $\alpha/4\pi$ that are smooth in $(a_{U}, x, y)$ and independent of $\varepsilon$; the Jacobian stays nonsingular, so by the implicit function theorem the same conclusion holds for the full two-loop system near the stored solution (argued, not checked). The running of $f$ itself only enters through the average $\langle\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger})\rangle$, so no further datum appears.

\emph{(iii)} $x(\varepsilon)$ is a ratio of affine functions; the check extracts $dx/d\varepsilon$ at $\varepsilon = 0$ exactly ($\tfrac{2373195393}{977158000}$, $\tfrac{605922228}{274711375}$, $\tfrac{129038993}{47922750}$) and, with $d\ln M_{I} = 2\pi\,dx$ and $\varepsilon = \mathrm{Tr}/16\pi^{2}$, $d\ln M_{I}/d\,\mathrm{Tr}(ff^{\dagger}) = (dx/d\varepsilon)/8\pi$, bounded with certified rational bounds on $\pi$ into $(0.09, 0.10)$, $(0.08, 0.09)$, $(0.10, 0.11)$. Moving $\alpha_{s}$ by $\pm 0.0009$ from the input $59/500$ moves $\ln M_{I}$ by $\mp(0.03$ to $0.05)$ (computed: $-0.0365/+0.0371$, $-0.0334/+0.0339$, $-0.0401/+0.0407$). synthesis.untuned-fit-caps-lightest-heav.formal:
For any complex $3 \times 3$ Dirac matrix $M_{D}$ and complex symmetric invertible Majorana matrix $M_{R}$ with smallest Takagi value $\alpha$ (the lightest heavy neutrino mass), the light matrix $m_{\nu} = M_{D}^{\mathsf{T}}M_{R}^{-1}M_{D}$ has largest Takagi value $m_{3} \le \lVert M_{D}\rVert^{2}/\alpha$, so
\[
\alpha \;\le\; \frac{\lVert M_{D}\rVert^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\le\; \frac{9\,e^{2}}{m_{3}}, \qquad e = \max_{ij}\,|(M_{D})_{ij}|.
\]
On the untuned fit among the representative fits of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.fits-record-level}, which rest on Premise (EW) (Dirac entries at most $0.04$ GeV at $M_{I}$, nothing cancelling), with $e \le 0.045$ GeV and $m_{3}(M_{I}) \ge 25$ meV (a factor two below the record's lower end, as allowance for running), $\alpha < 7.3 \times 10^{8}$ GeV, which lies below the chain's $M_{I} = 1.9 \times 10^{10}$ GeV (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chain}) by a factor above $26$. Under Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy}, $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le \alpha$, with $\alpha$ read as the fit's lightest heavy mass, the descent on that fit reheats below $7.3 \times 10^{8}$ GeV and below the intermediate scale. Then the dark-matter remainder $\Omega h^{2} = \Omega_{c}h^{2} - \Omega_{b}h^{2}$ cannot be a relic of gravitational production from the plasma at the rate of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}, with quanta no heavier than the bath (the odd towers' seeding signpost of the dark-matter paper), unless the summed production coefficient $c$ of its light content exceeds $3.9 \times 10^{12}$; for any $c \le 1$ the seeding temperature exceeds the cap more than $1400$-fold. The fit's tuned rows (Dirac entries $2.2$, $2.9$, $4.0$ GeV) give by the same bound only $\alpha < 8.9$, $15.4$, $29.2 \times 10^{11}$ GeV at $m_{3} = 49.4$ meV, which with the running allowance do not decide even at $c = 1$.
synthesis.untuned-fit-caps-lightest-heav.technical:
In any seesaw, the heaviest light neutrino mass is bounded by the square of the Dirac matrix's norm divided by the lightest heavy neutrino mass, so the lightest heavy mass is at most the Dirac norm squared over $m_{3}$, and the norm of a three-by-three matrix is at most three times its largest entry. One representative fit of the Standard-Model paper, the untuned one, made under Premise (EW), keeps every Dirac neutrino entry below $0.04$ GeV at the intermediate scale. Allowing a factor two for the running of $m_{3}$ to that scale, the lightest heavy neutrino lies below $7.3 \times 10^{8}$ GeV, more than twenty-six times below the intermediate scale $1.9 \times 10^{10}$ GeV.

If the descent reheats below the lightest heavy neutrino, as the neutrino paper's Premise (R) states, then on that fit it reheats below $7.3 \times 10^{8}$ GeV and below the Pati-Salam breaking scale. The odd towers' remainder of the dark matter then cannot have been made by gravitational production from the plasma with quanta no heavier than the bath unless the hidden light content's summed production coefficient exceeds $3.9 \times 10^{12}$; for any content with coefficient up to one (several hundred vector species) the required temperature exceeds the cap more than a thousandfold. The fit's tuned rows, with Dirac entries of $2$ to $4$ GeV, give weaker bounds that do not decide. The fits rest on Premise (EW), not on Hypothesis (U), and identifying the neutrino paper's lower heavy scale with the fit's lightest heavy mass joins two papers' objects.
synthesis.untuned-fit-caps-lightest-heav.lay: In the seesaw picture, the ordinary neutrino masses are tiny because they are suppressed by very heavy partner neutrinos. A simple matrix inequality turns this around: given how large the neutrinos' ordinary (Dirac) mass terms are, the lightest heavy partner cannot be heavier than a definite amount. In one representative fit of the Standard-Model paper, the one that needs no fine cancellation, those mass terms are small, at most a few hundredths of a GeV, which puts the lightest heavy partner below about a billion GeV. The neutrino paper assumes the early universe never got hotter than that partner's mass, so on this fit the early universe stayed below about a billion GeV, far too cool for gravity alone to have made the hidden matter that would account for the rest of the dark matter.

proofs.main:
\emph{The norm inequality.} Write $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ for the operator norm; for a complex symmetric matrix it is the largest Takagi value, and $\lVert M_{R}^{-1}\rVert = 1/\alpha$ with $\alpha$ the smallest Takagi value of $M_{R}$ (in the Takagi form $M_{R} = U^{\mathsf{T}}DU$, $U$ unitary, $D$ diagonal non-negative, $M_{R}^{-1} = U^{-1}D^{-1}U^{-\mathsf{T}}$ and unitaries preserve the norm). Submultiplicativity and $\lVert M_{D}^{\mathsf{T}}\rVert = \lVert M_{D}\rVert$ give $m_{3} = \lVert m_{\nu}\rVert \le \lVert M_{D}\rVert^{2}/\alpha$. The operator norm is at most the Frobenius norm, and a $3 \times 3$ matrix with entries of modulus at most $e$ has Frobenius norm at most $3e$. Hence $\alpha \le 9e^{2}/m_{3}$. A rank-one Dirac matrix with a single entry in the row of the lightest heavy state attains $\lVert m_{\nu}\rVert = \lVert M_{D}\rVert^{2}/\alpha$.

\emph{The untuned fit.} Proposition \claimref{standard-model.fits-record-level} lists representative fits under Premise (EW); for the fit with $10$s, $126$ and $120$ in which the second family's factor three comes through mixing with the third and nothing cancels, a largest Dirac neutrino entry of $0.04$ GeV at $M_{I}$, with $m_{3}$ run to $M_{I}$ in the Standard Model. We take $e \le 0.045$ GeV (the rounding) and, rather than compute the running, allow $m_{3}(M_{I}) \ge 25$ meV, half the record's lower end $49.4$ meV. Then $\alpha \le 9e^{2}/m_{3} = 7.29 \times 10^{8}$ GeV, and $M_{I}/\alpha > 26$ for $M_{I} = 1.9 \times 10^{10}$ GeV, the two-loop intermediate scale of the chain with the $(15,2,2)$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chain}(4)).

\emph{The seeding requirement.} With rate per volume $c\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$ (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}, $M_{P} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}$ GeV), entropy density $s = (2\pi^{2}/45)g_{s}T^{3}$ and $H = \sqrt{\pi^{2}g_{*}/90}\,T^{2}/M_{P}$ in radiation domination, the comoving yield obeys $dY/dT = -c\,T^{8}M_{P}^{-4}/(sHT)$, so $Y = c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}/(3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3})$ with $\kappa_{s} = \sqrt{\pi^{2}g_{*}/90}\,(2\pi^{2}/45)g_{s}$, which at $g_{*} = g_{s} = 100$ lies in $(145.2, 145.3)$ for $\pi > 333/106$; this is the yield of T14's Appendix A. Allowing the factor $2$ on the yield that the rate's provenance absorbs, and quanta of mass $m \le T_{\mathrm{desc}}$, the mass per unit entropy of the relics is at most $2c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4}/(3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3})$. The remainder, $\Omega_{c}h^{2} - \Omega_{b}h^{2} \ge 0.1188 - 0.02252 = 0.09628$ (Planck 2018, one standard error each), has mass per unit entropy $(\Omega h^{2})(\rho_{c}/h^{2})/s_{0} > 3.508 \times 10^{-10}$ GeV. So $c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4} \ge A/2$ with $A = 3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3} \times 3.508 \times 10^{-10}$ GeV, evaluated with $\kappa_{s} = 145.2$: $A > 2.2068 \times 10^{48}$ GeV$^{4}$. With $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le \alpha$ (Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy}, $\alpha$ read as the fit's lightest heavy mass) this needs $c \ge A/(2\alpha^{4}) > 3.9 \times 10^{12}$, and $A/2 > (1400\,\alpha)^{4}$, so at $c \le 1$ the required temperature exceeds the cap more than $1400$-fold.

\emph{The tuned rows.} With entries $2.2$, $2.9$, $4.0$ GeV and $m_{3} = 49.4$ meV the bound gives $\alpha < 8.9$, $15.4$, $29.2 \times 10^{11}$ GeV; with the running allowance each fourth power exceeds $A/2$, so the crude bound does not decide those rows even at $c = 1$.

The check verifies the trace form of the inequality on exact instances (for real diagonal $M_{R}$ and integer $M_{D}$, $\mathrm{tr}\,m_{\nu} \le \lVert M_{D}\rVert_{F}^{2}/\alpha$, with equality exactly on the rank-one instances), $\kappa_{s}$ from its formula, and every number above in rational arithmetic.
